posts.topic: 340 unread messages
posts.why: A number every busy seller recognises with a wince.

tiktok.hook: This business has 340 unread messages.
tiktok.vo: This business has three hundred and forty unread messages. That is not a conversation, it is a queue to its own shop. Reading them, most are the same four questions. Put those four answers on the profile and the queue shrinks by half without you typing anything new.
tiktok.cap: 340 unread messages is not popularity. It is a queue blocking your own door.

slides: Price · delivery · hours · how to order
instagram.cap: Your inbox is telling you what your profile should say.

facebook.body:
If you have hundreds of unread messages, that is not popularity. It is a queue blocking your own door.

Open the last fifty and count how many ask the same four things: price, delivery, opening hours, how to order.

Almost all of them do.

Put those four answers on your profile and in your away message. The queue shrinks by half and nobody had to type anything new.

How many unread do you have right now? Be honest.

posts.topic: Seen is the most expensive word
posts.why: One word does the emotional work of the whole lesson.

tiktok.hook: "Seen" is the most expensive word in Nigerian business.
beats: It is not a read receipt
They think you don't want them
tiktok.vo: Seen is the most expensive word in Nigerian business. To you it means I will get to it. To them it means this business does not want my money. Even a broken reply beats a read receipt, because a read receipt is a decision you did not mean to make.
tiktok.cap: A blue tick with no reply is a no, whether you meant it or not.

instagram.cap: If you cannot answer now, answer with when you will.

facebook.body:
'Seen' is the most expensive word in Nigerian business.

To you it means 'I will get to it tonight'. To the customer it means 'this person does not want my money'.

A short reply that says when you will answer beats a blue tick every time. 'I can confirm by 6pm' costs four seconds and keeps the customer.

Do you reply even when you have no answer yet?

posts.topic: The follow-up that is not begging
posts.why: Removes the shame that stops people from following up at all.

tiktok.hook: The second message feels like begging because it asks for something.
tiktok.vo: The second message feels like begging because most second messages only ask. So add something instead. A delivery date. A photo of the thing. A note that you only have two slots left this week, if that is true. Once the message carries information, it is no longer begging, it is a service.
tiktok.cap: Begging asks. Following up gives. Add one useful thing.

instagram.cap: If the message carries no new information, do not send it.

facebook.body:
Most people do not follow up because the second message feels like begging.

It feels that way because it usually only asks: 'just checking in'.

Add something. A delivery date. A photo of the finished thing. A note that you have two slots left this week, if that is actually true.

Once the message carries information, it stops being begging and starts being a service.

What do you normally say in a second message?

posts.topic: Ghosting is a system failure
posts.why: Takes the blame off the customer and puts it where they can fix it.

tiktok.hook: Your customer did not ghost you. Your system did.
tiktok.vo: Your customer did not ghost you, your system did. Nobody was assigned to answer after six p.m. Nobody set a date when the quote went out. Nobody noticed the chat had gone quiet for three days. Ghosting feels like a rude person. It is usually an unowned gap.
tiktok.cap: Nobody owns the gap. That is the whole story.

instagram.cap: Assign the gap before you blame the customer.

facebook.body:
We call it ghosting, as though the customer did something to us.

Usually it is a system failure. Nobody was assigned to answer after 6pm. Nobody put a date on the quote. Nobody noticed the chat had gone quiet for three days.

Fix the gap, not the customer.

Who in your business owns the messages after hours?

posts.topic: The ₦90,000 order lost to four hours
posts.why: A single specific number makes the abstract lesson real.

tiktok.hook: She lost a ninety thousand naira order in four hours.
tiktok.vo: She lost a ninety thousand naira order in four hours. The customer messaged at nine in the morning. She was in the market, saw it, thought I will answer when I sit down, and replied at one. The customer had already ordered from the next chat. It was not a price problem. It was a four hour problem.
tiktok.cap: Four hours. Ninety thousand naira. Not one word about price.

instagram.cap: The most expensive thing in your business is not your price. It is your delay.

facebook.body:
She lost a ₦90,000 order in four hours.

A customer messaged at 9am. She was in the market, saw it, and thought she would answer when she sat down. She replied at 1pm. The customer had already ordered from the next chat in the list.

Not a price problem. Not a product problem. A four-hour problem.

What is the longest a customer waits for you on a normal day?

posts.topic: The three-day callback is one sentence
posts.why: So small that there is no excuse not to do it.

tiktok.hook: The three-day callback is one sentence long.
tiktok.vo: The three-day callback is one sentence long. Not a paragraph, not an apology, not just checking in. One line that assumes nothing: still need this for the weekend? If yes, they answer. If no, they tell you. Either way you stop guessing and you stop waiting.
tiktok.cap: One line. No apology. A question with a real answer.

instagram.cap: Send it on day three. Then leave them alone.

facebook.body:
The three-day callback is one sentence long.

'Still need this for the weekend?'

Not a paragraph. Not an apology for disturbing them. Not 'just checking in', which invites a polite nothing.

One line with a real question. They answer yes or no, and either way you stop waiting and guessing.

When did you last follow up on a quote?

posts.topic: 'Ok' is not a yes
posts.why: A tiny exchange that quietly kills hundreds of sales a week.

tiktok.hook: You sent the price. They said "ok".
tiktok.vo: You sent the price. They said ok. That is not a yes, and it is not a no. It is nothing yet, and most businesses leave it there. Reply with the next step in one line: should I send the payment details. Now you find out.
tiktok.cap: "Ok" is a pause, not a decision. Someone has to move.

instagram.cap: The next message is yours. Send one line with a next step in it.

facebook.body:
You send a price. The customer replies 'ok'.

That is not a yes. It is not a no. It is nothing yet, and most businesses leave it exactly there and count it as a sale that fell through.

Send one line with a next step in it: 'Should I send the payment details?' Now you find out in four seconds instead of four days.

What do you do when a customer says 'ok'?

posts.topic: Why did you stop replying?
posts.why: The answers remove the excuse that it was about money.

tiktok.hook: Why did you stop replying to a vendor?
beats: I saw it and got busy
tiktok.vo: Why did you stop replying to a vendor? I forgot, said one. I saw it at work and never came back, said another. I did not even realise I had not replied. Three answers and not one of them was about price. They did not reject you. They forgot you, which is worse, and easier to fix.
tiktok.cap: Nobody here rejected anybody. They forgot. Which is worse, and easier to fix.

instagram.cap: Silence is almost never a no. It is a busy person with 40 newer messages.

facebook.body:
I asked people on the street why they stopped replying to a vendor.

'I forgot.' 'I saw it at work and never came back.' 'I didn't even realise I hadn't replied.'

Not one of them said it was too expensive.

They did not reject you. They forgot you. Which is worse, and also much easier to fix, because a reminder costs nothing.

Do you send the reminder, or wait to be remembered?

posts.topic: If they vanish after the price
posts.why: Names the exact moment the buyer recognises.

tiktok.hook: If customers vanish right after the price, this is for you.
beats: It fixes chats you already have
tiktok.vo: If customers vanish right after the price, this is for you. Thirty-six scripts for the moments that cost you sales: price questions, let me think about it, delivery, payment, and silence. Plus a tracker so no follow-up is forgotten. Five thousand naira, do it yourself. No consulting, no guarantees, but it will not bring you new customers.
tiktok.cap: It fixes the customers already messaging you. ₦5,000. Message PLAYBOOK on WhatsApp: 0905 069 0837.

instagram.cap: No consulting. No guarantees. Just the words for the moments you keep getting wrong.

facebook.body:
If customers vanish right after you send the price, this is the one pack I would point you to.

Thirty-six scripts for the awkward moments: the price question, 'let me think about it', delivery, payment, and plain silence. Plus a tracker so no follow-up gets forgotten.

₦5,000. Do it yourself.

The honest limit: no consulting, no guarantees, and it will not bring you a single new customer. It only helps with the ones already messaging you.

Message PLAYBOOK on WhatsApp: 0905 069 0837.

posts.topic: No to the blast, yes to eleven messages
posts.why: Shows the alternative to automation without moralising.

tiktok.hook: A client asked us to automate his follow-ups. We said no.
beats: So we wrote eleven personal messages
tiktok.vo: A client asked us to automate his follow-ups. We said no, and it was not a principle, it was arithmetic. A broadcast to two thousand people would save him an hour and look exactly like what it was. So we wrote eleven personal messages to the eleven real enquiries and he sent them by hand. Forty minutes. Four replies the same day.
tiktok.cap: We are not against automation. We are against it being the first thing.

instagram.cap: Automate the tenth time, not the first. By then you know what works.

facebook.body:
A client asked us to automate his follow-ups.

We said no, and it was not a principle, it was arithmetic. A broadcast to 2,000 contacts would save him an hour and look exactly like what it was. Most of them would ignore it.

So we wrote eleven personal messages to the eleven real enquiries and he sent them by hand. Forty minutes. Four replies the same day.

Automate the tenth time. Not the first.

Would a broadcast even work on your customers?

posts.topic: Log every enquiry with a date
posts.why: The unglamorous habit behind every good sales story in this month.

tiktok.hook: The most profitable thing in your business is a column of dates.
tiktok.vo: The most profitable thing in your business is a column of dates. Every enquiry, the name, what they asked, and the date you will next speak to them. Open that sheet every morning and work the rows that are due. You will find sales you had already written off, sitting in a chat nobody reopened.
tiktok.cap: Name, what they asked, next date. Four columns and a habit.

instagram.cap: Every sales story in this account comes back to one spreadsheet.

facebook.body:
The most profitable thing in a small business is a column of dates.

Name. What they asked for. The date you will speak to them next.

Open that sheet every morning and work the rows that are due today. That is the whole system.

You will find sales you had written off sitting in chats nobody reopened.

Do you have this sheet, or is it all in your head?

posts.topic: A homepage about the founder
posts.why: Painfully common, and everyone can see their own version.

tiktok.hook: This homepage describes the founder and never says what they sell.
tiktok.vo: This homepage describes the founder and never says what they sell. Three paragraphs about passion, starting from a small idea, and one line about excellence. Zero products, zero prices, zero next step. Nobody came for your passion. They came to find out whether you sell the thing they need.
tiktok.cap: Nobody ever bought a business because the founder was passionate. They bought a thing.

instagram.cap: Product first. Story second. That way people who are not here for the story still buy.

facebook.body:
A lot of Lagos homepages spend three paragraphs on the founder and never say what the business sells.

Passion. The journey. A small beginning. Commitment to excellence.

Zero products. Zero prices. Zero next step.

Nobody arrives at your site for your passion. They arrive to find out whether you sell the thing they need. Tell them that first. The story can come second, and more people will read it.

What is the first thing on your homepage?

posts.topic: The About page is doing the homepage's job
posts.why: A structural insight that reframes where the work goes.

tiktok.hook: Your About page is doing the homepage's job, and neither is working.
tiktok.vo: Your About page is doing the homepage's job. The homepage should say what you sell and what to do next. The About page should say who you are. Instead the homepage tells your story and the About page is the only place with a product on it. Swap them back and watch enquiries move.
tiktok.cap: Homepage sells. About page explains. Most sites have them the wrong way round.

instagram.cap: Check yours tonight. It takes one minute.

facebook.body:
A structural thing most small business sites get wrong: the homepage and the About page have swapped jobs.

The homepage is busy telling your story. The About page is the only place with a product on it.

It should be the other way round. Homepage: what you sell, who for, what to do next. About page: who you are, why you started.

Swap them. Same words. Different order. Different results.

Have a look at yours and tell me which one has the product on it.

posts.topic: The sentence a customer would say
posts.why: The fastest route to a headline that sounds human.

tiktok.hook: Your headline is hiding in something a customer already said to you.
beats: The sentence they use to describe you
tiktok.vo: Your headline is already written. It is the sentence a customer uses to describe you to a friend. Not the words you chose, the words they used. Ask three customers: how would you describe what we do. Take the clearest answer and put it on the page. It will sound more like your business than anything you write about yourself.
tiktok.cap: Ask three customers how they describe you. Put the clearest answer on the page.

instagram.cap: Your customers already wrote your headline. You just have not asked.

facebook.body:
Your headline is probably already written. It is sitting in someone's chat history.

Ask three customers: 'How would you describe what we do, to a friend?'

Take the clearest answer and put it on your homepage, word for word. It will sound more like your business than anything you write about yourself, because you are too close to it.

Try it this week. Three messages.

What do you think they would say?

posts.topic: 'A wide range of services'
posts.why: Nails a phrase every Nigerian business uses and no customer believes.

tiktok.hook: "We offer a wide range of services" means you are not sure.
beats: A stranger reads it as not for me
It is a list, not a promise
tiktok.vo: We offer a wide range of services means you are not sure what you are. A stranger reads that and hears not for me. It is a list, not a promise. Pick the one service that pays your rent, lead with it for a month, then add the second one.
tiktok.cap: "Wide range" is a shrug with extra words.

instagram.cap: Lead with the one that pays rent. Add the rest later.

facebook.body:
'We offer a wide range of services tailored to your needs.'

That sentence means the business is not sure what it is, and a stranger reads it as 'not for me'.

It is a list, not a promise.

Pick the one service that pays your rent. Lead with it for a month. Then add the second one once people know you for the first.

What would you lead with if you had to choose one?

posts.topic: One sentence doubled the enquiries
posts.why: The before and after makes the lesson impossible to dismiss.

tiktok.hook: A man described his business in one sentence and his enquiries doubled.
beats: He had been hiding it in paragraph four
We moved it to the top
tiktok.vo: A man described his business in one sentence and his enquiries doubled. The sentence already existed on his site, in paragraph four, under a photo. We moved it to the top, made it bigger, and changed nothing else. Same site, same photos, same price. It had been there the whole time, in the wrong place.
tiktok.cap: The sentence already existed. It was just in paragraph four.

slides: We moved it to the top
instagram.cap: Most businesses do not need new words. They need the right words moved up.

facebook.body:
A man described his business in one sentence and his enquiries doubled.

The sentence already existed. It was on his site, in paragraph four, under a photo of the team.

We moved it to the top, made it bigger, and changed nothing else. Same site, same photos, same prices.

It had been there the whole time, in the wrong place.

Go and read your own paragraph four. Is that your headline?

posts.topic: One product, one price, one next step
posts.why: A starting point for businesses with nine products and no focus.

tiktok.hook: If your page has nine products, pick one and hide eight.
tiktok.vo: If your page has nine products, pick one and put the other eight below it. For thirty days, one product, one price, one button at the top. You are not deleting anything, you are choosing an order. The other eight are still there for people who scroll, and most of your new customers will not scroll.
tiktok.cap: You are not deleting the other eight. You are choosing what a stranger sees first.

instagram.cap: Order is a decision. Most pages never make one.

facebook.body:
If your page has nine products, a stranger cannot pick one, so they pick none.

For thirty days, put one product at the top. One price. One button. Everything else sits below it.

You are not deleting anything. You are choosing an order, and order is the decision most pages never make.

Which one would you put at the top?

posts.topic: Your name says nothing
posts.why: Reassurance plus a rule, which is the most saveable combination.

tiktok.hook: Your business name does not say what you do. That is fine.
tiktok.vo: Your business name does not say what you do, and that is fine, because most do not. What has to say it is the first line under the name. Six words. Then the name works, because it is being explained by the only thing a stranger reads first.
tiktok.cap: Names are for memory. The first line is for understanding.

instagram.cap: Nobody needs a new name. They need one line under it.

facebook.body:
Your business name does not say what you do, and that is fine — most do not.

What has to say it is the first line underneath. Six words.

'Bread, baked at 6am, Agege.' 'Ankara tailoring, ready in five days.'

Then the name works, because it is being explained by the only thing a stranger actually reads.

What is your six words?

posts.topic: I read them the homepage only
posts.why: The failure is measured in public, which makes it undeniable.

tiktok.hook: I read people a homepage and asked what the business sells.
beats: Two out of ten got it right
Five said they did not know
tiktok.vo: I read ten people a homepage and asked what the business sells. Two got it right. Three guessed a completely different kind of business. Five said they did not know, and one asked whether it was a school. The owner had spent money on that page and this is the result. It is not a design problem. The page never says the thing.
tiktok.cap: Ten strangers. Two correct answers. That is your conversion rate, before anyone clicks.

instagram.cap: Read your homepage to ten strangers. You will learn more than any analytics tool will tell you.

facebook.body:
I read ten people a homepage and asked what the business sells.

Two got it right. Three guessed a completely different type of business. Five said they did not know, and one asked if it was a school.

The owner had paid money for that page.

It is not a design problem. The page never says the thing. Read yours to ten people this week — not friends, strangers — and count the correct answers.

What do you think yours would score?

posts.topic: For the first screen only
posts.why: Scoping the pack down makes it easier to say yes to.

tiktok.hook: This pack fixes one thing: the first screen.
tiktok.vo: This pack fixes one thing, and it is the first screen. Not your whole website, not your logo, not your traffic. What you say, who it is for, and what the button does. One evening of writing, no design skills needed. But if your problem is somewhere else, do not buy it.
tiktok.cap: First screen only. ₦5,000, one evening. Message CLEAR on WhatsApp: 0905 069 0837.

instagram.cap: Not your whole site. The first screen, which is where most sales are lost.

facebook.body:
This pack fixes exactly one thing: the first screen of your homepage.

Not your whole site. Not your logo. Not your traffic.

What you say, who it is for, and what the button does. One evening of writing. No design skills needed.

₦5,000. Message CLEAR on WhatsApp: 0905 069 0837.

If your problem is traffic, hosting or speed, this is not the pack for you, and I would rather tell you now.

Which one is actually your problem?

posts.topic: The site with no prices at all
posts.why: A testable claim, which is rarer and more persuasive than an opinion.

tiktok.hook: A client wanted a website with no prices anywhere.
beats: He was sure it looked expensive
We built one page with prices first
Then the rest as he wanted
tiktok.vo: A client wanted a website with no prices anywhere, because he was sure prices made him look cheap. So we built one extra page, with prices on it, and kept all the others clean. Three weeks in, the page with prices had four times the enquiries. He did not change his mind about how it looked. The customers did.
tiktok.cap: He did not want prices on his site. So we tested it on one page instead of arguing.

slides: We built one page with them
instagram.cap: Argue with a client and you get one unhappy client. Test it and you get an answer.

facebook.body:
A client wanted his new website to have no prices anywhere, because he was sure that prices made a business look cheap.

Instead of arguing, we built one extra page with prices on it and left the rest of the site exactly as he wanted.

Three weeks later, the priced page had roughly four times the enquiries of the rest combined.

He did not change his mind about how it looked. His customers did.

When you disagree with a client, do you argue or do you test?

posts.topic: Read it out loud
posts.why: A free test that surfaces every problem in ninety seconds.

tiktok.hook: Read your homepage out loud to someone who does not know you.
tiktok.vo: Read your homepage out loud to someone who does not know your business. Do not explain, do not add anything, just read it. Watch their face at the point where they stop following. That is the sentence to fix, and it is almost never the one you were worried about.
tiktok.cap: Watch their face, not their words. The polite ones will lie.

instagram.cap: Ten people, one page. You are looking for the sentence where the face changes.

facebook.body:
Read your homepage out loud to someone who does not know your business.

Do not explain anything. Do not add context. Just read it and watch their face.

There will be a point where they stop following. That is the sentence to fix, and it is almost never the one you were worried about.

Politeness will fool you if you ask them what they think. Faces do not lie.

Who could you read yours to this week?
